answer: Resist sybils by throttling the trust graph itself. A single admission kernel mints a hard-capped number of new vertices per epoch, and each scarce slot clears through a costly priority auction ratified by a rotating summit of established peers. Spinning up 1000 fakes then means either waiting dozens of epochs for the cap to release slots, or outbidding every honest newcomer at escalating marginal prices for one vertex the summit can still reject. Population cannot balloon past what the kernel admits, so a swarm pays in real time, capital, or both.
